verses.1: And there was a famine in the land, just as there had been before during the time of Abraham. Then Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines.
verses.2: And Jehovah saw him, and said, “Do not go back to Egypt, into that land that I told you about.”
verses.3: I will come to this land with you, and I will bless you. I will give you all the lands that belong to you and your descendants. I will establish the covenant that I made with your father Abraham.
verses.4: And I increased your descendants like the stars in the sky. I gave you all the lands of the earth, and all the nations of the earth were blessed through your descendants.
verses.5: For as Abraham heard from my mouth, he kept my commandments, laws, and ordinances.
verses.7: And they asked the people of that place about their wife. One of them said, “She is my wife; I don’t want to kill her.” But the people of that place refused to allow it, saying, “It’s better for her to die than to be with me.”
verses.8: And it happened that as those days passed, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, saw Rebecca, his wife. And he laughed at her.
verses.9: And Abimelech called to Isaac and said, “But behold, your wife is hers. And how did you say that she is my sister?” Isaac replied, “Because what I said is not true about her.”
verses.10: And Abimelech said, “What have you done to us? After all, one of our people had your wife as his wife, and you brought that woman upon us.”
verses.11: And Abimelech commanded all the people, “Whoever touches this man and his wife shall die.”
verses.12: And Isaac planted his seeds in that land. In that same year, he found a hundred fields. And Jehovah blessed him.
verses.13: And the man grew up, and he continued to grow in stature. He became much taller than anyone else.
verses.14: And he had a flock of sheep, as well as some cattle. He worked hard, but the Philistines hated him.
verses.15: And all the wells that the servants of his father dug during the time of Abraham’s father were filled with water. But these wells were later filled with salt, and they became useless.
verses.16: And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us! You have abandoned us after all.”
verses.17: And from there, Isaac went and settled in Nahal Garar. He lived there.
verses.18: And Isaac sat down and dug in the holes that had been dug out by his father Abraham. The Philistines dug those holes after Abraham’s death. They gave those holes names, just like the names that his father had given them.
verses.19: And the servants of Isaac dug in the valley, and they found there living water.
verses.20: And the sons of Gerar fought with the sons of Isaac. They said, “Give us the waters.” So they named the river Essek, because it became dry up along with them.
verses.21: And they dug in another well. They also fought over it. They called its name Shitna.
verses.22: And he went there again, and dug in another place. But they didn’t find much there. He named that place “Rahovot.” He said, “Now, may Jehovah expand our territory and make us prosperous on this land.”
verses.23: And he ascended from there in a ladder.
verses.24: And Jehovah saw him in that night, and said, “I am the God of Abraham, your father. Do not be afraid of me, for I am with you. I will bless your descendants through Abraham.”
verses.25: And he built there a altar. He named it after Jehovah. He also built his temple there. And he settled the servants of Isaac there.
verses.26: And Abimelech went to him from Gerar. He took possession of his land. As a result, the commander of the army became king.
verses.27: And Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me? You hate me, and yet you sent me away from among you.”
verses.28: And they said, “We have seen that Jehovah is with you.” And they said, “Let there be a covenant between us, between us and you, so that this covenant may be established with you.”
verses.29: If you do us any harm, while we have done nothing to you. And if we have only done good to you, and we send you away in peace. Then you are blessed, O Jehovah.
verses.30: And he prepared food for them, and they ate and drank.
verses.31: And they sat down in the morning. Each man sat with his brother. Then Isaac sent them away, and they left with peace.
verses.32: And on that day, the servants of Isaac came and told him about the springs they had found. They said to him, “We have found springs from the water.”
verses.33: And it was named “Shiv’a” because of this. The name of the city remains “Shiv’a” to this day.
verses.34: Esau was forty years old when he took a Jewish woman named Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and also Basmat, daughter of Eilon the Hittite.
verses.35: And she became a spirit to Isaac and Rebekah.
